query: how to draft email replies with ai and still check them
title: Draft email replies with AI and still check them | 50agents
description: Let AI draft your email replies and check each in under a minute: a five-point review of facts, promises, prices, dates and recipients before you send.
h1: How to draft email replies with AI and still check them
answer: Let the AI write drafts into the thread, never send, and check each one in under a minute against five things: facts, promises, prices and dates, recipients, and tone.
Give it your facts and two or three sample replies so the drafts sound like you, and correct it in words when it gets something wrong so the next draft is better.

body.p: Read every AI draft for these five, in this order. The first three are where the expensive mistakes hide.

head: Check
Look for
Why
rows: A draft can fill a gap with something plausible and wrong.
You are bound by what you send, not what you meant.
Old prices in memory, wrong year, wrong timezone.
A reply-all to a thread with a supplier on it.
Too stiff, too cheerful, too long
Matters least, and is easiest to fix.

body.p: Google’s help says Gemini "may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information". Every vendor says something similar. The review is not optional.

sections.h2: Make the drafts sound like you

ul: **Three real replies you liked**, pasted in as examples of tone and length.
**Your sign-off and greeting**, exactly as you write them.
**The facts it will be asked about**: prices, hours, policies, links. Kept somewhere the AI reads every time, and updated when they change.
**What you never say**: "unfortunately", discounts, legal opinions. Give the reason so it applies the rule sensibly.
**Corrections, in words.** When you change a draft, tell the tool why ("we never offer refunds by email, offer a call"). Lindy, for one, learns from your edits but needs you to save what it learned.

method.h2: How to set it up, step by step

steps.title: Choose which emails get drafts
steps.body: Questions from customers to support@, or all mail from people (not newsletters) to you. Narrow is better.

steps.title: Drafts only, never auto-send
steps.body: Drafts in the thread, or a card to approve. Turn off any auto-send setting before the first run.

steps.title: Load your facts and examples
steps.body: The list above. Without facts, the AI writes friendly replies that answer nothing.

steps.title: Tell it what to do when it does not know
steps.body: "If the answer is not in what you know, do not draft. Tell me what is missing." A gap you see is better than a guess you send.

steps.title: Review for two weeks, then decide
steps.body: Count drafts sent unchanged, edited, and thrown away. Fix the facts behind the thrown-away ones.

body: In 50agents an AI agent drafts replies from what your business knows (its memory, which you can read and correct), and every reply waits in Needs you with the full text. You can approve it as it is, change it, or decline it. Corrections you make in its chat become lessons it uses next time.

wrong.title: A promise you did not make
wrong.body: The draft offered a refund or a deadline. Keep policies in the AI’s facts and list what it may never offer.

wrong.title: Stale prices
wrong.body: Last year’s price in its memory. Update facts the day they change, and date them.

wrong.title: Reply-all to the wrong people
wrong.body: A thread with a supplier on Cc. Check recipients every time; it takes a second.

wrong.title: Auto-send left on
wrong.body: A setting you did not notice sent drafts on their own. Check before the first run, and again after any update.

wrong.title: Everything sounds the same
wrong.body: Generic drafts with no examples. Paste in three of your own replies.

faqs.q: Can AI reply to my emails for me?
faqs.a: It can draft them well. Sending should stay with you, at least for anything that reaches a customer.

faqs.q: How do I make AI emails sound like me?
faqs.a: Give it three replies you wrote and liked, your exact greeting and sign-off, and correct it in words when it misses.

faqs.q: Should I tell people a reply was drafted by AI?
faqs.a: If you read and approve it, it is your reply. If something goes out unreviewed, say so, or better, do not let it.
